root_cause.text: nci_close_device() in the NFC NCI subsystem incorrectly flushed rx_wq while holding ndev->req_lock, even though nci_rx_work can re-enter the request path and acquire the same req_lock, creating a circular locking dependency and deadlock risk.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “nci_close_device() flushes rx_wq and tx_wq while holding req_lock” and shows the lock-taking path “nci_rx_work -> ... -> nci_request -> mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock)”; the patch removes flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) from the locked section and moves it after mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock) with the comment “rx_work may take req_lock via nci_deactivate_target”.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid flushing the RX workqueue during device close under lock, while still flushing TX work, to prevent incorrect shutdown behavior.
intent_record.what: The code changes the workqueue flushing in nci_close_device() by removing the call to flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq), keeping only flush_workqueue(ndev->tx_wq), and updating the comment from "Flush RX and TX wq" to "Flush TX wq, RX wq flush can't be under the lock".
intent_record.how: At runtime, device close no longer attempts to flush the RX workqueue while this code path is executing under the current lock context, avoiding an unsafe or invalid RX workqueue flush there while still ensuring pending TX work is drained.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify close-path comments to accurately describe remaining rx activity and the scope of the workqueue flush.
intent_record.what: The comment above ndev->ops->close(ndev) was changed from stating that the queues are empty and no works are scheduled to stating that rx work may still be running but will observe that NCI_UP was cleared, and the later comment before flush_workqueue(ndev->cmd_wq) was updated from "Flush cmd wq" to "Flush cmd and tx wq".
intent_record.how: This diff does not alter executable code or control flow; it clarifies the actual runtime state during device close by documenting that rx work can still be active after NCI_UP is cleared and that flushing cmd_wq also covers tx work handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Flush the RX workqueue during device close to prevent pending receive work from racing with shutdown and reentering req_lock.
intent_record.what: A comment and a call to flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq) were added in nci_close_device() after mutex_unlock(&ndev->req_lock) and before returning 0.
intent_record.how: This makes device close wait until all pending rx_wq work has finished executing, preventing concurrent rx work from continuing after close and avoiding lock-related races because that work may later acquire req_lock through nci_deactivate_target.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is directly visible in `nci_close_device()`. The function acquires `ndev->req_lock` with `mutex_lock(&ndev->req_lock);` near the start, and while still holding that lock it executes `flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq);` (and also `flush_workqueue(ndev->tx_wq);`). The root cause states that flushing `rx_wq` while holding `req_lock` is unsafe because `nci_rx_work` can re-enter the request path and try to acquire the same `req_lock`, causing a circular dependency/deadlock. This commit contains exactly that construct. The worker body is also shown: `nci_rx_work()` processes incoming packets via `nci_rsp_packet(ndev, skb);`, `nci_ntf_packet(ndev, skb);`, and `nci_rx_data_packet(ndev, skb);`, so RX work clearly runs asynchronously and can invoke broader request-handling logic. There is no mitigation in `nci_close_device()` such as releasing `req_lock` before `flush_workqueue(ndev->rx_wq)` or otherwise preventing RX work from taking that lock. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not present.
